correctness.rationale: The edge boundary-value solution independently gives Λ_G(k²)=k/sin(kℓ)(A-cos(kℓ)D). At an odd resonance the finite factor tends to Q=D+A and the scalar residue magnitude tends to 2λ0/ℓ, hence the scaled least singular value tends to (2λ0/ℓ)q_min(Q). At even resonance the factor tends to -L, which has a constant-vector kernel. For fixed d, Q(G)+Q(Gbar)=(d-2)I+J; on the orthogonal complement of the all-ones vector this gives q_min(G)<=d-2, and any missing complement edge produces a strict test vector, so equality is unique to K_d. A fresh independent enumeration of every simple graph through five vertices reproduced unique maxima 1,2,3 for d=3,4,5.

originality.rationale: Originality passes narrowly. Do--Kuchment--Ong prove only existence of an unspecified uniform pole constant under their resonance condition and explicitly ask how that constant depends on the decoration in order to choose effective designs. The audited result answers that stated design question on the natural all-boundary equilateral simple-graph subclass by identifying the exact residue with the least signless-Laplacian eigenvalue and solving the fixed-boundary-size optimization. Standard signless-Laplacian theory supplies graph-spectral ingredients but no checked source couples them to this quantum-graph pole coefficient.
